summary.text: Lloyd Smucker is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 11th District, first elected in 2016. He owned a Lancaster County commercial construction company for 25 years, served on his township's planning commission and board of supervisors, and was a Pennsylvania state senator from 2009 to 2016. He serves on the House Committees on Ways and Means and the Budget, where his official biography lists him as vice chair.

paragraphs.text: Born January 23, 1964, in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. In a campaign announcement he said he was born Amish, one of 12 children.
Graduated from Lancaster Mennonite High School in 1981 and attended Lebanon Valley College and Franklin and Marshall College.

Was president and owner of the Smucker Company, a family-owned commercial construction firm in Smoketown, for 25 years. In a campaign announcement he said he bought a drywalling business at age 17; his official biography says the company grew to employ more than 150 people.
Served on the West Lampeter Township planning commission (2001-2005) and board of supervisors (2005-2009).
Served in the Pennsylvania State Senate for the 13th District from 2009 until he resigned on November 30, 2016, chairing the Senate Education Committee.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and took office in 2017, first in the 16th District and, after the 2018 redistricting, in the 11th. He won re-election in 2022 over Democrat Bob Hollister, 62%-38%.
Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Subcommittees on Trade, Social Security and Tax) and the Committee on the Budget, where his official biography lists him as vice chair.
Renominated without opposition in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. His official biography says he lives in Lancaster County with his wife.
